To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the steady-state levels in cultured hypothalamic and brainstem neurons of AT2 receptor mRNAs are regulated by NGF and insulin.
the angiotensin type 2 (AII) receptor gene promoter is responsive to growth factors, including nerve growth factor ( NGF ), insulin, and phorbol ester.
the steady-state levels and subcellular distribution of angiotension II type 2 receptors (AT2Rs) in rat brain are developmentally regulated and are regulated in vitro by growth factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of the AT2 receptor.
the role of the AT2 receptor in the developing and adult CNS.
the identification of growth factors and cytokines which modulate the expression of the angiotensin type 2 receptor (AT2R) in the CNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AT2 receptors may be important for the development and differentiation of the brain.
growth factors can modulate AT2 receptor mRNA expression and this may be important in the development and differentiation of the brain.
NGF and PMA increase AT2 receptor mRNA expression, whereas insulin decreases AT2 receptor mRNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGF and Insulin can regulate the AT2 receptor in neuronal cultures derived from neonatal CNS, but the mechanisms are not fully understood.
the angiotensin AT2 receptor may be a novel target for growth factor action.
the AT2-receptor is involved in the development and differentiation of neurons in the CNS, and that the expression of this receptor is modulated by a variety of growth factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AT2 receptor mRNA is expressed in neurons derived from the rat hypothalamus/brainstem, and the expression of this gene is regulated by growth factors.
AT2 receptor mRNA is regulated by a complex array of factors, which may include growth factors, hormones and neurotransmitters.
the AT2 receptors are involved in development and differentiation of the central nervous system.
